messages:
Amira Patel: Quick debrief from the red-team run on zodiac-lite v0.9 (int8) — ran jailbreak_v2 suite across 1k prompts, attaching topline numbers below
Jonah Kim: nice, link to raw results?
Amira Patel: Uploaded to /mnt/runs/zodiac-lite/2026-03-20/jb-v2-1000.csv and summary in thread. TL;DR: overall JB success 6.2% (int8), baseline fp16 run 1.0% — clear regression after quant.
Samir Rao: whoa that's >6x. Is this concentrated on a few templates or spread out?
Amira Patel: concentrated: 70% of successes from 3 prompt families (persona escalation, role-swap, and chain-of-thought tricking). Most failures trigger when the model produces >2 uninterrupted reasoning tokens.
Lina Chen: did you run with the same prompt pre-processing and temperature? quant can interact with sampling.
Amira Patel: yes same pipeline/seed. Params: temp=0.0, top_p=0.95, max_tokens=256. Repro command:
```
redteam-run --model zodiac-lite-int8 --suite jailbreak_v2 --seeds 0-999 --batch 32 --temp 0.0 --out summary.json
```
Jonah Kim: any pattern in logits/softmax? quantization can change logit spacing.
Amira Patel: looked at delta-logit histograms — shift ~0.6 std for next-token probability on prompted sequences with long context. Also KV-cache hits slightly lower (miss rate +4%). Suspect precision loss in KV accumulation for long chains.
Samir Rao: could be kernel selection for GEMM path on the int8 build. Which runtime/commit?
Amira Patel: runtime: rwinf 2.3.1, kernels: cuda-12-custom-int8-v4 (commit 9f3b2). QA note: int8 build used AOQ scaling override.
Lina Chen: can you run quick A/B: int8 with alternative kernel (v3) and int4 fallback? want to see if regression correlates to kernel or bitwidth.
Amira Patel: already ran quick A/B: int8-v3 -> 3.1% JB; int4 (experimental) -> 8.9% JB. So v4 kernel worse than v3, and int4 much worse overall.
Jonah Kim: so two failure modes: kernel v4 numeric instability, and lower bitwidth amplifies failure. Are there any prompt truncation artifacts? maybe KV index misalignment causes context shift.
Amira Patel: we observed occasional token duplication mid-response (small %). Example snippet from a single fail (sanitized):
```
User: ...
Model: Step 1: do X. Step 1: do X. Then do Y...
```
Samir Rao: duplication likely points to KV cache or position embedding mismatch after quant step. Can we repro with deterministic seed and inspect KV tensors?
Amira Patel: yes, plan: run a focused repro on the top 10 prompts with debug-level KV dumps. Need infra slot with 24GB and int8 debug build.
Lina Chen: allocate on dedicated infra, I'll open a ticket to reserve a gpu. Also flagging security: escalate to policy team? higher JB rate is material.
Amira Patel: agreed — @policy-team please FYI. For next steps:
1) repro KV dumps on v3 and v4 kernels (top 10 prompts)
2) run kernel-level unit tests on int8 accumulation paths
3) revert to kernel v3 on canary traffic + monitor JB rate
4) add red-team regression check to CI for quantized bring-ups
Jonah Kim: +1 on CI check. Also add a small eval that counts token duplications and refusal flips.
Samir Rao: I'll take item 2 and 4. Amira, assign me the repro artifacts path.
Amira Patel: Done — artifacts at /mnt/runs/zodiac-lite/jb-repro/2170001111/, KV dump flag enabled in run manifest.
Lina Chen: quick mitigation: enable strict-refusal postfilter for canary and lower max_tokens to 128 until we root cause.
Amira Patel: applied strict-refusal filter on canary, reduced max_tokens. Early telemetry shows JB drop from 6.2% -> 1.8% on canary.
Jonah Kim: good catch. Can we schedule a quick sync tomorrow 10am to triage kernel patch? I'll invite infra and runtime.
Amira Patel: scheduled. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
